# Ctxo MCP Server — Full Reference

> AI agents don't fail because they can't code. They fail because they code blind. Ctxo gives them the full picture before they write a single line.
> npm: @ctxo/cli | GitHub: https://github.com/alperhankendi/Ctxo

## Setup

```bash
npm install -g @ctxo/cli      # One-time global install (gives you the `ctxo` command)
ctxo init                     # Rules, skills, guard, MCP config, git hooks, plugins
ctxo index                    # Build codebase index (required once)
ctxo index --check            # CI gate: fail if index stale (writes nothing, records no snapshot)
ctxo index --commit HEAD      # Re-index the files one commit changed (what the post-commit hook runs)
ctxo index --files a.ts b.ts  # Re-index only these files (alias: --file <path>)
ctxo                          # Start MCP server (stdio transport)
ctxo install domain           # opt-in domain knowledge layer (@ctxo/domain)
ctxo init --domain            # registry skeleton, fold guard hooks, skill, domain config
ctxo verify-domain --since origin/main   # CI gate for contexts, cards, rule IDs, boundaries
```

MCP client configuration:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ctxo": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@ctxo/cli"] } } }
```

---

## Monorepo & Plugin Architecture (v0.7+)

Ctxo is a pnpm workspace monorepo:

- `@ctxo/cli` (packages/cli) - CLI entry, composition root, MCP server, tool handlers
- `@ctxo/plugin-api` (packages/plugin-api) - `CtxoLanguagePlugin` protocol interface (v1 and v2)
- `@ctxo/lang-typescript` - ts-morph (full tier) plugin for TS/JS
- `@ctxo/lang-go` - ctxo-go-analyzer (full tier, Go 1.22+) + tree-sitter plugin for Go
- `@ctxo/lang-csharp` - Roslyn plugin for C# (attribute annotations; SQL edges at known call sites when `@ctxo/lang-sql` is installed)
- `@ctxo/lang-java` - tree-sitter Java plugin (syntax tier); full tier via `@ctxo/lang-java-analyzer` companion package (JRE 11+ required)
- `@ctxo/lang-sql` (packages/lang-sql) - T-SQL plugin for `.sql` files, protocol v2 (`ctxo install sql`, alias `tsql`)
- `@ctxo/sql-extract` (packages/sql-extract) - zero-dependency T-SQL tokenizer and recognizers; a library, not a plugin, never discovered

Plugin protocol (`CtxoLanguagePlugin`):
- `apiVersion`: `'1'` or `'2'`, the lowest version the plugin works on. The CLI accepts both (`SUPPORTED_API_VERSIONS = ['1', '2']`) and handles their output identically; `'1'` stays accepted for at least 12 months after `'2'` ships. The official plugins declare `'1'`; `@ctxo/lang-sql` declares `'2'`.
- `id`: unique plugin identifier
- `extensions`: file extensions handled (e.g. `['.ts', '.tsx']`)
- `tier`: `'syntax'` | `'full'`
- `createAdapter(ctx)`: factory returning an `ILanguageAdapter` instance
- v2 additions (all additive): the data kinds, `SymbolNode.annotations`, optional `extractFacts`, and `ctx.capabilities` (`facts`, `sqlCallSites`). See "Plugin Protocol v2, Data Coupling and SQL" below.
- Dependencies: plugins import only from `@ctxo/plugin-api`; the one exception is `@ctxo/sql-extract` (ADR-017).

Discovery: at startup Ctxo scans the project's `package.json` dependencies for names matching `@ctxo/lang-*` or `ctxo-lang-*` and registers them. `ctxo install` adds plugins; `ctxo index --install-missing` auto-installs plugins required by detected languages. New CLI: `ctxo doctor --fix`, `ctxo version`, and `ctxo --version --verbose|--json` for plugin/runtime diagnostics.

Source paths referenced below live under `packages/cli/src/`.

---

## Tool Reference (14 core tools, plus 4 with @ctxo/domain: 18)

### get_logic_slice
Retrieve a symbol and all its transitive dependencies.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, optional): Symbol ID (format: file::name::kind)
- symbolIds (string[], optional): Batch: array of symbol IDs
- level (number 1-4, default 3): L1=signature, L2=direct deps, L3=full closure, L4=with token budget
- intent (string, optional): Filter dependencies by keyword

Nodes carry their `annotations` (C# attributes, SQL table `columns`) at L4 only; L1-L3 omit them (and nodes from the SQLite fallback have none). A 2-part data ID such as `dbo.usp_closeloan::procedure` walks the body of the winning definition; a copy's full ID walks that copy's own body.

When to use: Understanding what a symbol depends on (downstream view).
Instead of: get_blast_radius (upstream/impact), get_context_for_task (task-specific).

### get_blast_radius
Find all symbols that would break if a target changes.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, required): Symbol ID, or the 2-part ID of a table, view or procedure (`dbo.loans::table`)
- confidence (enum: confirmed|likely|potential, optional): Filter by tier
- intent (string, optional): Filter by keyword

Returns: impactedSymbols array with symbolId, depth, riskScore, confidence, edgeKinds, coChangeFrequency (when the dependent's file co-changes with the target's file).
3-tier model by the strongest edge that reaches each dependent: confirmed (calls/extends/implements and the data edges reads/writes/executes), likely (uses/co-changed), potential (imports-only). A potential dependent whose file co-changes with the target's file at frequency above 0.5 is promoted to likely. The traversal is transitive across all tiers; riskScore falls with depth.
overallRiskScore = sum(riskScore) / (sum(riskScore) + 5) over all impacted symbols (riskScore = 1 / depth^0.7): it approaches 1 but never reaches it. low < 0.3, medium 0.3-0.7, high > 0.7; 1 direct dependent scores about 0.17, 3 about 0.38 (medium), 12 about 0.71 (high).
Also returns coChangedFiles (when co-change data exists): up to 10 files that co-change with the target's file at frequency >= 0.5 but have no graph path to it, each with file, frequency, sharedCommits. Informational: not counted in tiers, risk scores or the safe-edit gate.
Every copy of a table, view or procedure that several files define, and its 2-part ID, reports the same dependents (those of the winning definition).

With @ctxo/domain and a domain graph: `rulesAffected` (card rules linked to the target or an impacted symbol, target first; each `{ ruleId, title, context, card, via: [{ symbolId, link: code|test }] (up to 5), viaCount }`) and `cardsToUpdate` (`{ context, card }`, registry order). Capped at 50 with `<name>Total`.

When to use: BEFORE modifying any symbol, including a SQL table, view or procedure.
Instead of: get_logic_slice (forward deps), get_pr_impact (PR-level).

### get_architectural_overlay
Get project architectural layer map.

Parameters:
- layer (string, optional): Filter by layer name
- mode (enum: both|regex|communities|contexts, default both): "regex" layer map, "communities" Louvain clusters, "contexts" candidate bounded contexts (file level), "both" layers plus communities
- candidate (number, optional): With mode "contexts", the id of one candidate to return in full

Returns: Symbols grouped into Domain, Infrastructure, Adapter, Test, Composition, Configuration layers; with communities, data-driven clusters and god nodes. With mode "contexts", a summary: `commitSha`, `coverage`, `candidates` (`id`, `label`, `fingerprint`, `fileCount`, `cohesion`, top 5 `topTerms`), `hubs` (capped at 50, with `hubsTotal`), `collisions` (capped at 50, with `collisionsTotal`), `unclustered` count and a `hint`. Data coupling appears in the summary as counts only: `sharedTableCount` on each candidate that has shared tables, plus `dataResourcesTotal`, `sharedResourcesTotal` (resources of two or more candidates) and `externalResourcesTotal` (resources no `.sql` file defines). With `candidate: <id>`, that candidate in full (files capped at 15 with `fileCount`, cross-candidate edges, co-change pairs, `sharedTables` with `sharedTableCount`), its hubs (50), its collisions (10, each with only that candidate's own occurrences: `symbolId`, first 5 members, `memberCount`) and its own `dataResources` with `dataResourcesTotal`. `sharedTables`: the first 15 by name, each `{ name, kind?, external, accesses: [{ candidate, modes }], owner?, accessCount }` with up to 10 accesses (the asking candidate's own access always kept). `dataResources`: the first 15 by name, each `{ name, kind?, external, modes, owner?, writerCount }`. When the detail is still larger than the response limit, trailing entries are dropped by name order from the longer of the two lists (dataResources on a tie); the counts keep the totals. An unknown id or no contexts view returns `found: false` with a hint (run `ctxo index`). `ctxo contexts --json` prints the full artifact.

When to use: Onboarding to a new codebase, validating layer boundaries, preparing a context map (mode "contexts").

### get_why_context
Retrieve git commit history and anti-pattern warnings for a symbol.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, required): Symbol ID
- maxCommits (number, optional): Limit to N most recent commits

Returns: commitHistory array + antiPatternWarnings (reverts, rollbacks, undo patterns), and driftSignals when a community snapshot exists. driftSignals carries confidence (low below 3 distinct commits, medium 3-6, high 7+), distinctCommits (different commits in the snapshot history, other than the current one), snapshotsAvailable (history entries passed in, kept for compatibility) and an optional hint.

With @ctxo/domain and a domain graph: `decisions`, up to 5 dated card decisions of the symbol's context (those naming a rule linked to the symbol first, each group newest first; `decisionsTotal` when more), each `{ id, date, text, card, line, rules, provenance }`; provenance entries are `{ kind: "file", path, exists, label? }` or `{ kind: "external", value }` (never fetched). `[]` when the file has no single owning context.

When to use: Understanding WHY code was written this way, checking for problem history.
Pair with: get_change_intelligence (complexity/churn scores).

### get_change_intelligence
Retrieve complexity x churn composite score.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, required): Symbol ID

Returns: complexity (0-1), churn (0-1), composite (0-1), band (low|medium|high|critical).

When to use: Identifying refactoring targets, assessing modification risk.

### find_dead_code
Find unreachable symbols and files.

Parameters:
- includeTests (boolean, default false): Include test files
- intent (string, optional): Filter results by keyword

Returns: deadSymbols (with confidence 1.0/0.9/0.7 and reason), deadFiles, unusedExports, scaffolding markers. Symbols in .sql files are never reported (their consumers may live outside the index).

Test files are decided by the shared test-file classifier (the default test globs, such as `**/*.test.*`, `**/*_test.go` and `**/src/test/**`, plus files where a test-framework annotation marks a symbol). Unless includeTests is set they are left out: test symbols are never reported, and production code called only from tests is not dead.

When to use: Cleanup, refactoring, confirming code is truly unused.
Instead of: find_importers (specific symbol reverse lookup).

### get_context_for_task
Get task-optimized context for a symbol.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, required): Symbol ID
- taskType (enum: fix|extend|refactor|understand, required): Determines context mix
- tokenBudget (number, default 4000): Max tokens

Task types:
- fix: History + anti-patterns + direct deps (bug investigation)
- extend: Deps + blast radius + interfaces (adding features)
- refactor: Importers + complexity + churn (restructuring)
- understand: Full slice + architecture (learning)

Context entries that depend on the symbol (its blast radius) carry an optional confidence tier (confirmed|likely|potential); co-change history can raise potential to likely. Entries carry no symbol annotations (use get_logic_slice level 4). A 2-part data ID (`dbo.loans::table`) is accepted.

With @ctxo/domain and a domain graph: `cardExcerpt` `{ context?, card?, rules: [{ ruleId, title, linkedTo: target|neighbour, text? }], terms: [{ term, definition }], contracts?, tokens, omitted }`. Up to a quarter of tokenBudget is reserved before the code context is packed; the excerpt fills tokenBudget - totalTokens, so the sum never exceeds the budget. Left out only when even an empty excerpt does not fit.

When to use: BEST starting point when you know the symbol AND your intent.

### get_ranked_context
Search and rank symbols by relevance to a query.

Parameters:
- query (string, required): Natural language search query
- tokenBudget (number, default 4000): Max tokens for results
- strategy (enum: combined|dependency|importance, default combined): Ranking strategy
- searchMode (enum: fts|legacy, default fts): "fts" is BM25 with camelCase splitting, trigram fallback and automatic typo correction (reported in `fuzzyCorrection`); "legacy" is substring matching

- scope (enum: code|domain, default code; only with @ctxo/domain): "domain" searches rules, terms, decisions, card sections and in-repo provenance files (BM25 k1 1.2, b 0.75, no PageRank; strategy and searchMode do not apply). Without the package the parameter does not exist.

Returns: Symbols ranked by BM25 relevance + PageRank importance, packed within budget. With scope "domain": `{ query, scope, results: [{ id, kind: rule|term|decision|section|provenance, title, context?, path, line?, excerpt, relevanceScore, tokens }], totalTokens, tokenBudget, searchMetrics }`.

When to use: Have a question/topic but don't know which symbol to look at.
Instead of: search_symbols (exact name/regex search).

### search_symbols
Search symbols by name or regex pattern.

Parameters:
- pattern (string, required): Substring or regex pattern
- kind (enum: function|class|interface|method|variable|type|table|view|procedure, optional): Filter by kind (table, view and procedure come from SQL plugins)
- filePattern (string, optional): Filter by file path substring
- limit (number 1-100, default 25): Max results
- mode (enum: regex|fts, default regex): "regex" is a case-insensitive regex or substring match on names; "fts" is BM25 relevance search with typo correction

When to use: Know (part of) the symbol name, need its ID for other tools.
Instead of: get_ranked_context (semantic/relevance search).

### get_changed_symbols
Get symbols in recently changed files.

Parameters:
- since (string, default HEAD~1): Git ref to diff against
- maxFiles (number, default 50): Max files to process

When to use: See what was modified in recent commits.
Instead of: get_pr_impact (full PR risk assessment).

### find_importers
Find all symbols that depend on a given symbol (reverse dependency).

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, required): Symbol ID, or the 2-part ID of a table, view or procedure (`dbo.loans::table`; every copy gives the same importers)
- edgeKinds (string[], optional): Filter by imports|calls|extends|implements|uses|reads|writes|executes (the last three are data access)
- transitive (boolean, default false): Follow transitive reverse edges
- maxDepth (number 1-10, default 5): Max BFS depth
- intent (string, optional): Filter by keyword

When to use: Check if safe to modify/delete, find all consumers.
Instead of: get_blast_radius (aggregated impact with risk scores).

### get_class_hierarchy
Get class inheritance hierarchy.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, optional): Root symbol (omit for full project)
- direction (enum: ancestors|descendants|both, default both): Traversal direction

When to use: OOP code, understanding type relationships before modifying base class/interface.

### get_symbol_importance
Rank symbols by PageRank centrality.

Parameters:
- limit (number 1-200, default 25): Max results
- kind (enum: function|class|interface|method|variable|type|table|view|procedure, optional): Filter (PageRank runs on the whole graph, data edges included)
- filePattern (string, optional): Filter by file path
- damping (number 0-1, default 0.85): PageRank damping factor

When to use: Identify most critical symbols, high-risk modification targets.
Instead of: find_dead_code (unused/unimportant code).

### get_pr_impact
Analyze PR impact in a single call.

Parameters:
- since (string, default HEAD~1): Git ref to diff against
- maxFiles (number, default 50): Max files
- confidence (enum: confirmed|likely|potential, optional): Filter tier

Returns: changedFiles, changedSymbols, totalImpact, riskLevel (low|medium|high), per-file blast radius, co-change data (coChangedWith per file), boundaryViolations (confidence from distinctCommits) and clustersAffected.
riskLevel comes from the highest per-symbol overallRiskScore = sum(riskScore) / (sum(riskScore) + 5) (see get_blast_radius): high > 0.7 (about 12 or more direct dependents), medium > 0.3 (about 3), else low. A symbol with one or two dependents is low.

With @ctxo/domain and a domain graph: `contextsTouched` (`{ id, status, card?, cardChanged, acknowledged?, fileCount, files }` with up to 10 files; over the merge base of since and HEAD plus the working tree, while `files` stays `git diff <since>`), `cardsChanged` (registry cards changed in the range or the working tree) and `rulesWithoutTests` (rules of touched contexts without a test link, with `untested` reasons). Capped at 50 with `<name>Total`; left out when git cannot resolve since. An empty diff also carries `_meta`.

When to use: FIRST tool when reviewing a PR or evaluating recent commits.

### get_domain_context (with @ctxo/domain)
The card of the named context that owns a symbol or file.

Parameters:
- symbolId (string, optional): Symbol ID; its file part selects the context (the symbol need not be indexed). Wins over path
- path (string, optional): Repo-relative file path, or a context's card path

Returns: `context` (id, name, rung, card, rulePrefix, paths), `terms` (definitions with origin card|glossary, up to 15 `identifiers`, `identifierCount`), `rules` (each with `untested?`, up to 10 `tests` and 10 `code` links with `sources`, `testCount`, `codeCount`), `contracts` (outbound, inbound, text, references), `decisions` (newest first, capped at 50) and `openQuestions`. With neither parameter: `contexts` with ruleCount, rulesWithTests, termCount, decisionCount. Misses: `{ found: false, hint }` (no registry, invalid or changed registry, no graph, no owning context, a path outside the project). After a card edit not yet indexed: `stale: true` and a hint.

When to use: Before changing code in a named context; to learn the rules, terms and contracts behind it.

### get_rule (with @ctxo/domain)
One domain rule by ID.

Parameters:
- ruleId (string, required): e.g. LEND-03; LEND03, Lend03, lend_03 and the id of a domain-scope hit (rule:LEND-03) also match

Returns: `rule` (ruleId, title, text, line, untested?, context, card), `tests` and `symbols` (each `{ file, symbolId?, testName?, fallback?, sources: [{ source, annotation?, file, line }] }`; test sources annotation|category|test-title|rule-comment|mention|card-tests, code sources card-code|rule-comment), `decisions` mentioning it, `provenance` (with the decision it came from) and `unresolved` card values when any. `{ found: false, hint: "No rule <ID> in any card." }` for an unknown ID.

When to use: A change may affect a business rule; find the tests that pin it and the decisions behind it.

### find_shadow_specs (with @ctxo/domain)
Shadow-spec candidates of a named context: business-looking logic no card rule pins yet (the Deletion Test).

Parameters:
- context (string, required): context ID from the registry, e.g. lending
- kinds (string[], optional): any of literal-comparison, normalization, retry-timeout, endpoint, data-resource, procedure, rule-without-tests; omitted or empty means all kinds
- includeResolved (boolean, optional, default false): also return resolved candidates with their resolution

Returns: `context` (id, name, rung), `counts` (`open`, `resolved`, `byKind: { <kind>: { open, resolved } }` for kinds with candidates), `shadowSpecs` (each `{ fingerprint, kind, file, line (1-based), symbolId? | ruleId?, text, detail?, source: native|text|index|card, resolution? }`; resolution `{ by: "rule-link", rules }`, `{ by: "untested", reason }`, `{ by: "shadow-specs", rule }` or `{ by: "shadow-specs", notARule }`), `resolutionFile` (the context's shadow-specs.yaml path), `staleResolutions` (`{ fingerprint, line }`), `unknownRules` (`{ fingerprint, rule, line }`), `resolutionProblems` (`{ line, severity, message }`); the last three capped at 50 with `<name>Total`, never summed (an unknown-rule entry matching nothing is in both). Fingerprint `kind | symbol | normalized text`: copy it verbatim into shadow-specs.yaml as a YAML single-quoted scalar (`fingerprint: '...'`, a `'` inside written `''`); `%7C` and `%25` in the kind and symbol parts are an encoded `|` and `%` (`%7c` matches too). Misses: `{ found: false, hint }` (no registry, registry problems, unknown context, no loop artifacts, also when the last ctxo index built the graph but not the candidates or maturity facts and removed both: run ctxo index). Stale artifacts: `stale: true` and a hint. Under ctxo watch, candidates refresh only on the next ctxo index.

When to use: Running the Deletion Test on a context: for each open candidate, find or write the rule that pins it (get_rule), or record why it is not a rule in shadow-specs.yaml.

### get_context_map (with @ctxo/domain)
The map of named contexts with a suggested rung.

Parameters: none.

Returns: `contextMap` (per context in registry order: id, name, rung, suggestedRung, card { path?, present }, rules { count, withTests, share }, tests { characterization, contract }, crossContextEdges { in, out }, coChange { pairs, top }, drift (or null), boundaryViolations { total, errors, warnings }, shadowSpecs { open, resolved }, criteria { pinned, named, bounded, boring } each with `met` and its counts, boundariesKnown), `summary` (contexts, agree, suggestedAbove, suggestedBelow), `settings` (pinnedCoverage). Without boundaries.json: `boundariesKnown: false`, bounded not met, and a hint. While `domain.rules.trackerPrefixes`, `domain.tests.ruleTraitKeys`, `domain.tests.characterization` and `domain.tests.contract` are all at their defaults and the last `ctxo index` found that discovery would add something (`maturity.json` `discovery.addsSomething`), the hint also says to run `ctxo domain discover`; the "no registry" and "no domain graph" hints name it too. `contextMap` is truncatable; `ctxo domain map --json` prints it whole.

When to use: How mature is each context, and what blocks its next rung?

---

## Tool Selection Guide

```
Reviewing a PR or recent changes?
  -> get_pr_impact (single call, full risk assessment)

About to modify a function or class?
  -> get_blast_radius (what breaks if I change this?)
  -> then get_why_context (any history of problems?)

Need to understand what a symbol does?
  -> get_context_for_task(taskType: "understand")
  -> or get_logic_slice (L2 for overview, L3 for full closure)

Fixing a bug?
  -> get_context_for_task(taskType: "fix")

Adding a feature / extending code?
  -> get_context_for_task(taskType: "extend")

Refactoring?
  -> get_context_for_task(taskType: "refactor")

Don't know the symbol name?
  -> search_symbols (by name/regex)
  -> get_ranked_context (by natural language query)

Onboarding to a new codebase?
  -> get_architectural_overlay (layer map)
  -> get_symbol_importance (most critical symbols)

Preparing a context map?
  -> get_architectural_overlay(mode: "contexts") (candidate bounded contexts)
  -> then candidate: <id> for one in full

Cleaning up code?
  -> find_dead_code (unused symbols)
  -> get_change_intelligence (complexity hotspots)

Checking if safe to delete/rename?
  -> find_importers (who depends on this?)
  -> get_blast_radius (full impact)

Working with class hierarchies?
  -> get_class_hierarchy (extends/implements tree)

Need the business rules or decisions behind code? (with @ctxo/domain)
  -> get_domain_context (the card of the context that owns the symbol or file)
  -> then get_rule (one rule: tests, code, decisions)

Running the Deletion Test? (with @ctxo/domain)
  -> find_shadow_specs (business logic no rule pins yet), then get_rule

How mature is each context? (with @ctxo/domain)
  -> get_context_map (metrics, suggested rung, criteria)
```

---

## Cross-Cutting Features

### Response Envelope (_meta)
All tool responses include:
```json
{ "_meta": { "totalItems": 50, "returnedItems": 25, "truncated": true, "totalBytes": 12400, "hint": "Use search_symbols to narrow results." } }
```
- Default truncation threshold: 8KB
- Configurable via CTXO_RESPONSE_LIMIT environment variable
- In `get_architectural_overlay` mode "contexts", only `candidates` is truncatable (hint: use `candidate: <id>` or `ctxo contexts --json`); `hubs` and `collisions` are capped at the source and never truncated. In the `candidate: <id>` detail, `sharedTables` and `dataResources` are not truncatable either: they are capped at 15 each and shortened from the end until the detail fits the limit, with `sharedTableCount` and `dataResourcesTotal` keeping the totals

### Intent Filtering
4 tools accept `intent` parameter: get_blast_radius, get_logic_slice, find_importers, find_dead_code.
- Keywords extracted from intent string, matched case-insensitively against symbolId, file, name, kind, edgeKind, reason
- Multiple keywords use OR logic
- No intent = full results (backward compatible)

### Symbol ID Format
All symbols use deterministic IDs: `"<relativePath>::<name>::<kind>"`
- Example: `"src/core/graph/symbol-graph.ts::SymbolGraph::class"`, `"db/lending.sql::dbo.loans::table"`
- Valid kinds: function, class, interface, method, variable, type, table, view, procedure
- Valid edge kinds: imports, calls, extends, implements, uses, reads, writes, executes
- Edge targets may also be 2-part name references (`<name>::<kind>`); data edges point at canonical names such as `dbo.loans::table` (lowercase, delimiters stripped, default schema `dbo`), resolved to the defining `table` or `view`. With several definitions, the winner is a copy outside test files (default test globs; `index.tests` is not consulted), then outside `docs`/`doc`/`documentation` folders, then the codepoint-smallest symbol ID
- Impact tools (get_blast_radius, find_importers, get_pr_impact, get_context_for_task, the gate, `ctxo blast-radius`) accept a 2-part data ID and give every copy of a multi-defined object the winner's dependents; forward edges (get_logic_slice) stay per copy; get_why_context with a 2-part ID reads the winner's file

### Resources
- `ctxo://status` — Health check resource (confirms server is running)

---

## Co-change, Incremental Indexing and Snapshots (v0.13, #157)

Co-change (files that change together in git history) feeds every blast-radius path: get_blast_radius, get_pr_impact, get_context_for_task, `ctxo blast-radius`, the gate hook and `ctxo gate --preview`.

### The co-change window

Built by `ctxo index` from one `git log --no-merges -M --name-status` pass over the commits reachable from HEAD. The same pass fills each file's `intent[]`, and both follow renames. The window is independent of `--max-history` (which only limits commits kept per file in `intent[]`, default 20). Config in `.ctxo/config.yaml` (all optional):

```yaml
cochange:
  maxCommits: 2000        # last N non-merge commits from HEAD, or "all"
  # since: 12m            # also limit by age; d, w, m, y; counted back from HEAD's committer date
  maxFilesPerCommit: 30   # commits touching more analysed files are skipped (massSkipped)
  minShared: 2            # shared commits needed for a pair
  include: []             # extra tracked, non-indexed files to analyse (globs)
  exclude: []             # indexed files to leave out (globs); also vetoes include-added files
```

- CLI overrides: `ctxo index --cochange-commits <n|all>`, `ctxo index --cochange-since <duration>` (30d, 2w, 12m, 1y).
- A pair becomes an entry at `shared >= minShared` and `frequency = shared / min(countA, countB) >= 0.1`. The applied window is recorded in `.ctxo/index/co-changes.json` under `window`; the file is only rewritten when entries or window change.
- `commitsScanned` counts every non-merge commit of the repository, so in a monorepo a numeric maxCommits covers fewer relevant commits than its value suggests.
- Sparse checkout: files outside the cone are absent from the matrix, and their committed index entries are never pruned.
- `ctxo verify-index` reports files with a rename in their history as STALE until the next `ctxo index` after upgrading, because `intent[]` now follows renames.

### Incremental indexing and the post-commit hook

- `ctxo index --files <path...>` (alias `--file <path>`) re-indexes the listed files. `ctxo index --commit <rev>` re-indexes the files one commit changed and removes the ones it deleted or renamed away. Both load the symbol registry from the committed index and compute co-change, communities, the snapshot, the drift and boundary artifacts and the SQLite cache from the merged index. Candidates pass the same filters as a full run.
- A full `ctxo index` uses only the files it discovers and prunes index entries of deleted or newly ignored sources (never of skip-worktree paths).
- `ctxo init` installs a versioned post-commit block (`# ctxo-start v2`) that runs `ctxo index --commit HEAD` once per commit, guarded by `[ -d .ctxo ]`. `ctxo init` and `ctxo doctor --fix` upgrade an older block in place, collapse duplicate blocks, and follow `core.hooksPath`. A global or system `core.hooksPath` is shared by every repository, so ctxo writes nothing there and prints the blocks to add by hand (scope detection needs git 2.26+).
- `ctxo doctor` has a `git_hooks` check: warns on a missing, outdated or duplicated post-commit block.
- `ctxo <command> --help` (and `-h`) prints the help and runs nothing.

### One snapshot per commit

`.ctxo/index/communities.json` is the current snapshot and `communities.history/` keeps at most one earlier snapshot per commit. A second run on the same commit replaces the current snapshot without archiving. Drift compares against the newest history entry from a different commit. Drift and boundary confidence count `distinctCommits` (low below 3, medium 3-6, high 7+; boundary needs at least 2). `ctxo index --check` writes nothing and records no snapshot. The first write after upgrading removes older same-commit duplicates from `communities.history/`.

### Gate consequence

The safe-edit gate counts confirmed + likely dependents, so co-change-upgraded dependents count and the gate may fire somewhat more often. `ctxo gate --preview` shows the effect.

Design record: docs/architecture/ADR/adr-016-co-change-engine-and-snapshot-policy.md

---

## Contexts View (v0.13, #156)

Candidate bounded contexts, computed by `ctxo index` and written to `.ctxo/index/contexts-view.json` (committed). Louvain runs on a file graph whose edges blend dependency weight (distinct symbol edges, log-normalised) and co-change frequency; hub files (fan-in or god nodes) have their edges damped by `1 / log2(2 + dependents)` and are listed separately. Groups smaller than `minCandidateFiles` fold into a neighbour; files with no edge are `unclustered`. Each candidate has a suggested label (longest common directory; PageRank fallback at the repo root), a `fingerprint`, cohesion, top terms, cross-candidate edges and co-change pairs. Collisions are type names that appear in two candidates with different member shapes (Jaccard below 0.5). No domain is named automatically.

Refresh: every index run that re-indexes files (full, `--files`, `--commit`, so also every post-commit hook run); skipped by `--skip-community`; not refreshed by `ctxo watch`.

Surfaces: `get_architectural_overlay({ mode: "contexts" })` (summary first, `candidate: <id>` for one in full) and `ctxo contexts [--json]` (table to stderr, full artifact to stdout; without a view it exits 0 with `found: false`).

Config in `.ctxo/config.yaml` (all optional, defaults shown):

```yaml
communities:               # symbol-level Louvain
  resolution: 1.0
  godNodeMinBridged: 3
  godNodeMaxResults: 25
contextsView:
  weights: { dependency: 1.0, coChange: 1.0, data: 0 }   # data: weight of data edges (0 = shared tables never merge candidates)
  exclude: []              # files left out of the file graph (globs)
  hubs: { auto: true, topPercent: 1, minDependents: 10, paths: [] }   # paths lose all their edges
  resolution: 1.0
  minCandidateFiles: 3
  technicalTerms: []       # replaces the default list (Service, Repository, Controller, Handler, Manager, Dto, Impl, Async)
index:
  tests: []                # extra test-file globs; test files are never graph nodes
  facts: false             # true asks plugins for code facts (protocol v2, index JSON only)
```

Design record and evidence: docs/architecture/ADR/adr-016-co-change-engine-and-snapshot-policy.md (addendum "Contexts view defaults (PR 1A)").

---

## Plugin Protocol v2, Data Coupling and SQL (v0.13, #156)

Two services can look independent in the graph while both write the same table. Phase 1 of the domain knowledge layer makes that data coupling visible. Feature doc: docs/features/domain-knowledge.md. Design record: docs/architecture/ADR/adr-017-plugin-protocol-v2-and-data-coupling.md.

### Protocol v2 (`@ctxo/plugin-api`)

- Kinds: `SYMBOL_KINDS` adds `table`, `view`, `procedure`; `EDGE_KINDS` adds `reads`, `writes`, `executes`; `DATA_RESOURCE_KINDS = ['table', 'view']` is what core analyses use.
- Annotations: `SymbolNode.annotations?: { name, args?, named? }[]`. Always on. Host-language attributes are capped at 20 per symbol, 10 positional entries and 10 named entries plus the reserved `type`, 200 characters per value; `named.type` is reserved for the fully qualified type name, and a source argument named `type` is not kept. lang-sql's `columns` annotation lists every column of a table. Core checks shape only; JSON index only.
- Facts: `FACT_KINDS = ['literal-comparison', 'normalization', 'retry-timeout', 'endpoint']`, `CodeFact { kind, symbolId, line (0-based), text (single line, trimmed, max 200 chars), detail? }`, optional `ILanguageAdapter.extractFacts`. Called only on a fact request (`index.facts: true`, or an installed `@ctxo/domain` whose registry file exists); results go to the file's index JSON under `facts` (`[]` when a fact-capable plugin finds nothing). The TypeScript, C#, Java and Go plugins implement it since PR 4 (see Fact Detectors below).
- Capabilities: `PluginContext.capabilities?: { facts?, sqlCallSites? }`, computed before any `createAdapter` call and offered to every plugin. `sqlCallSites` is set only when a plugin for `.sql` is installed.
- Versioning: `SUPPORTED_API_VERSIONS = ['1', '2']`; plugins declare the lowest version they work on. Older CLIs skip `@ctxo/lang-sql` with a warning and drop the new kinds from a newer index with a warning.

### `@ctxo/lang-sql`

- `ctxo install sql` (alias `tsql`). Syntax tier, no database, no .NET. Detection, `ctxo doctor` and `ctxo index --install-missing` suggest it when the repository has at least 5 `.sql` files that are also at least 2% of its files (as `git ls-files` lists them).
- Definitions: `CREATE [OR ALTER] TABLE | VIEW | PROC[EDURE] | FUNCTION`, `ALTER VIEW | PROC[EDURE] | FUNCTION`. Symbol IDs carry the canonical name (`db/lending.sql::dbo.loans::table`); `name` keeps the declared spelling. Functions map to `function`.
- Accesses from view, procedure and function bodies: `FROM`, `JOIN`, `APPLY`, `MERGE ... USING` -> reads; `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`, `SELECT ... INTO`, `OUTPUT ... INTO` -> writes; `EXEC` / `EXECUTE` -> executes. Temp tables, table variables, CTE names, aliases, 3- and 4-part names and the `sys` / `information_schema` schemas are skipped. Only ASCII A-Z is case-folded.
- Limits: T-SQL only with `dbo` as the default schema; top-level DML in scripts is skipped; `ALTER TABLE ... ADD` columns count only in the defining file; a CTE name reused later in a batch without `;` is skipped by sql-extract but read by ScriptDom.
- Size limit: a `.sql` file larger than 5 MiB is skipped (no symbols, edges or facts) with one warning per file: `skipped <file>: <n> MiB is over the 5 MiB SQL size limit`. Use `index.ignore` for dumps to silence it.
- Several definitions of one object (migrations, docs or test copies): see "Symbol ID Format" above for the winner; every copy reports the winner's dependents, each copy keeps its own forward edges, and the contexts view gives an executing candidate the bodies of every production copy of a procedure (the winner's alone when no copy is production; docs and test copies add nothing when a production copy exists). The winner among production copies is the codepoint-smallest path, not necessarily the newest migration (`V10__` sorts before `V7__`).

### SQL at C# call sites

With lang-sql installed and the Roslyn tier (.NET SDK 8+), the C# helper parses constant SQL with ScriptDom at: `SqlCommand` constructor `cmdText`; `CommandText` assignments on `SqlCommand`, `DbCommand`, `IDbCommand` and subtypes (a procedure name when `CommandType = StoredProcedure` is set on the same local or in the same object initializer); Dapper `SqlMapper` methods starting with `Query` or `Execute` (`sql` argument; `commandType: CommandType.StoredProcedure` means a procedure name); the Dapper `CommandDefinition` constructor (`commandText` argument; a named or positional `commandType` of `StoredProcedure` means a procedure name; the edge belongs to the method that constructs it); `SqlBulkCopy.DestinationTableName` (writes); EF Core `FromSqlRaw`, `ExecuteSqlRaw`, `ExecuteSqlRawAsync`, `SqlQueryRaw` (EF `{0}` placeholders become parameters before parsing). Only compile-time constants count: use `const string`; `static readonly` fields, runtime strings and `CommandText +=` are non-constant. Dapper `IN @ids` is read as `IN (@ids)`. The tree-sitter fallback gives no SQL edges. `DEBUG=ctxo:roslyn` logs the constant, non-constant and unparsable counts.

### C# annotations and test files

- The C# plugin reports attributes in both tiers. Roslyn keeps constant arguments (strings and characters as their value, numbers in invariant culture, booleans, enum constants as `Type.Member`, `typeof(T)` as a display string, arrays flattened, nulls skipped); tree-sitter keeps literal arguments only (strings, numbers, booleans). In the Roslyn semantic path a `name:` argument arrives in `args`; tree-sitter puts it in `named`. Roslyn formats real-number exponents its own way. A source argument named `type` is dropped in both tiers (`named.type` is reserved).
- Test files (contexts view): a test glob match, or any symbol carrying `Fact`, `Theory`, `SkippableFact`, `SkippableTheory`, `Test`, `TestCase`, `TestCaseSource`, `TestFixture`, `TestMethod`, `DataTestMethod` or `TestClass`. Once C# annotations exist in the index, a file matched only by `**/*Test.cs` or `**/*Tests.cs` needs a test annotation. Missed: test classes with only other attributes (FsCheck `[Property]`), custom attributes derived from `Fact` or `Theory` (names match exactly, base types are not resolved) and unannotated `*Tests.cs` in a bare capital `Tests/` or `Test/` folder (not a default test glob); fix with an `index.tests` glob.
- Run a full `ctxo index` after upgrading `@ctxo/lang-csharp`: an incremental run annotates only the files it re-indexes, while the contexts view already counts the index as annotated, so name-only test matches that were not re-indexed show up as production files until the full run.

### Data coupling in core and the contexts view

- `reads`, `writes`, `executes` are confirmed blast-radius dependents, so the safe-edit gate also guards heavily used tables and procedures. Data edges stay out of symbol-level communities, god nodes, cross-cluster counts and boundary violations. `.sql` symbols are never dead code.
- Contexts view artifact: top-level `dataResources` (`name`, `kind?`, `external`, `accesses` per candidate with `modes`, `writers`, `owner?` when exactly one candidate writes it) and per-candidate `sharedTables` (resources of two or more candidates). An `executes` edge to an indexed procedure adds that procedure's reads and writes, transitively; reading a view does not expand to its tables; unclustered files and test files are ignored and hubs count for their assigned candidate.
- Procedure attribution: procedure bodies count only for the candidates that execute them, decided by canonical name (no copy of an executed procedure credits its own candidate). With several definitions, an executing candidate takes the union of the bodies of every production copy (outside test files and `docs`, `doc` or `documentation` folders), or the winner's body alone when no copy is production; docs and test copies of a procedure that has a production copy add nothing. A procedure that no candidate executes, directly or through other procedures, credits the candidate whose file holds it (with several copies, the candidate of each production copy, or of the winner when none is production); procedures that only execute each other each credit their own candidate. A procedure that only tests or unclustered files execute therefore still credits the script's candidate.
- `contextsView.weights.data` (default 0) weights data edges between an accessing file and the defining `.sql` file in the file graph. At 0, a `.sql` file joins a candidate only through co-change, so scripts without a co-change partner stay unclustered and lower `coverage` (noticeably on one fixture, candidates unchanged); `contextsView.exclude` leaves them out. Table and view names and columns join the term harvest; tables take part in collisions with their columns, so a C# class and a same-name table can collide (often an entity mapped to its table: possible noise).
- `ctxo index` appends `, <S> shared tables` to its contexts line; `ctxo contexts` prints the count and one `shared` line per shared resource (owner, several writers or read only).
- Size: a table shared by k candidates is listed k times with k accesses each in the artifact (k squared growth); the MCP responses are capped.

### Doctor: `csharp_tier`

Five outcomes:
1. No C# sources: pass, "no C# sources detected".
2. No .NET 8+ SDK: pass, "syntax tier (install the .NET 8+ SDK for the full tier)".
3. `@ctxo/lang-csharp` not resolvable from the project: pass, "syntax tier (@ctxo/lang-csharp not installed)".
4. `dotnet restore` of the helper succeeds: pass, "full tier (.NET SDK <version>, Roslyn helper restores)".
5. The restore fails or times out (120 s): warn, "syntax tier: the Roslyn helper could not restore (<first error line>)". Fix: make `Microsoft.SqlServer.TransactSql.ScriptDom` and the `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis` packages reachable from your NuGet sources (nuget.org or a mirror), then run `ctxo index`.

When the helper cannot restore or build during `ctxo index`, the C# plugin falls back to tree-sitter (symbols and attribute annotations with literal arguments kept; `named.type`, non-literal argument values and SQL edges lost) and the summary reads `C#: N files (syntax tier - the Roslyn helper failed, run "ctxo doctor")`. In `ctxo watch`, a keep-alive that shut down for inactivity or crashed is restarted once on the next re-index; if that fails, the file falls back to tree-sitter instead of being written with zero symbols. The helper targets `net8.0` with `RollForward` `Major`, so the .NET host can roll forward to a newer major runtime when no 8.x is installed; the built helper has been run with `dotnet exec --fx-version` on .NET 8, 9 and 10. A lone `.csproj` without a solution now indexes in the Roslyn tier.

### Upgrade notes

- First re-index after upgrading rewrites the committed JSON of C# files once (annotations). Make it a full `ctxo index` (see "C# annotations and test files").
- UTF-16 files with a BOM are decoded; their hash changes once, so `ctxo index --check` reports them stale until the next `ctxo index`.
- Shared conformance corpus: packages/sql-extract/corpus (`<case>.sql` + `<case>.expected.json`, modes `statement` and `file`), run by sql-extract, lang-sql and (with .NET) ScriptDom.

---

## Language Parity: TypeScript, Java and Go (unreleased, #156 PR 1C)

`@ctxo/lang-typescript`, `@ctxo/lang-java` (with `@ctxo/lang-java-analyzer`) and `@ctxo/lang-go` do what `@ctxo/lang-csharp` does: annotations, tests as symbols with edges, and data edges for constant SQL at known call sites. Feature doc: docs/features/domain-knowledge.md ("Language parity"). Design record: the ADR-017 addendum.

### Capability matrix

| Language | Annotations (always on) | Test symbols | SQL at call sites (needs `@ctxo/lang-sql`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| C# | attributes, both tiers | test methods | Roslyn tier |
| TypeScript/JS | decorators | describe/it/test blocks | always (one tier) |
| Java | JDT: constant values; tree-sitter: strings only | test methods under src/test/java | JDT full tier only |
| Go | struct tags, both tiers | `_test.go` functions and methods (full tier) | analyzer full tier only |

### Known APIs

- TypeScript/JS (receiver must trace to the npm module): pg `query` (also `{ text }`); mysql2 `query`, `execute` (also `{ sql }`); mssql `query` (call or tagged template), `execute` (a procedure name); `knex.raw`; Prisma `$queryRaw`, `$executeRaw` (tagged template, interpolations become `@p0`, `@p1`) and `$queryRawUnsafe`, `$executeRawUnsafe`; TypeORM `query`; Sequelize `query`; better-sqlite3 `prepare`, `exec`.
- Java: JDBC `Connection.prepareStatement`, `prepareCall`, `Statement.execute*`; Spring `JdbcTemplate`, `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate` and their `*Operations` interfaces (`query*`, `update`, `batchUpdate`, `execute`); `EntityManager.createNativeQuery` (javax and jakarta); `@Query(value = ..., nativeQuery = true)`; MyBatis `@Select`, `@Insert`, `@Update`, `@Delete`. A JDBC escape `{call name(...)}` gives an `executes` edge.
- Go: `database/sql` `Query`, `QueryRow`, `Exec`, `Prepare` and their `Context` forms on DB, Tx, Conn, Stmt; sqlx `Select`, `Get`, `Queryx`, `NamedExec`, `MustExec` (methods and package functions); pgx v4 and v5 `Query`, `QueryRow`, `Exec`, including pgxpool; gorm `Raw`, `Exec`. The SQL is the argument bound to the callee's first `string` parameter.
- Out of scope in every language: ORM and query-builder calls (knex chains, Prisma model calls, TypeORM repositories, JPQL and Spring Data derived queries, gorm model calls).

### Constants and matching

- TypeScript: string literals, templates without substitutions, `+` and templates of constants, `const` bindings in the file or behind a relative import. Receiver provenance follows imports, `require`, type annotations and initializers, destructuring, constructor parameter properties and `this` members (through `extends` too), return types, `import('M').T`, `export *` barrels and dynamic `import()`, at most 8 steps. Relative modules missing from memory are read from disk (`.ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx`, inside the project root), so the post-commit hook, `--files` and watch give the same edges as a full run. Edges start at the innermost exported function, method of an exported class, exported variable or test block.
- Java: JDT constant evaluation (literals, static final fields, concatenation, text blocks). The owner matches the receiver's static type, the binding's declaring class or any supertype; without a binding, the declared type through the imports. Edges start at the enclosing method or constructor.
- Go: constants per `go/types`; the callee's method object (pointer stripped) names the owner. A closure belongs to its enclosing function.
- Non-constant SQL is counted (debug logs and the analyzers' `sql: { constant, nonConstant }` summary), never guessed, and never stored in the index.

### Annotation formats

- TypeScript: `name` is the rightmost identifier (`@nest.Injectable()` gives `Injectable`); `args` are string literal arguments; `named` holds string properties of object-literal arguments. Property decorators go on the class with `named.member` (`{ name: 'Column', named: { member: 'memberId', name: 'member_id' } }`). Accessor and parameter decorators are ignored.
- Java: simple name; `value` to `args`, other members to `named`; declared values only; strings, numbers, booleans, enum constants as `Type.MEMBER`, class literals as the qualified name; arrays flattened in `args` and joined with `,` in `named`. Java keeps a member named `member`.
- Go: `{ name: 'tag', named: { member: '<Field>', <key>: '<value>' } }` per tagged field, on the struct; `reflect.StructTag` rules, first key wins.
- Every language drops a key named `type` (`named.type` stays reserved).

### Test-block naming (TypeScript)

Title path joined with ` > `; whitespace collapsed; runs of `:` collapsed and a trailing `:` dropped; empty title `(untitled)`; cut at 200 characters; a repeated path (or one equal to an exported function name) gets ` #2`, ` #3`; children use their parent's final name. Example ID: `src/loans/loan-policy.test.ts::LoanPolicy > renewal > extends by seven days::function`. `index.tests` extras do not reach plugins.

### Effects and limits

- Tests count as blast-radius dependents (the gate may fire more often on well-tested symbols); symbol-level communities shift once; Go full-tier runs type-check test packages; JDT `calls`/`uses` edges stay type-level.
- find_dead_code: shared test-file classifier (default globs plus test-annotated files); test symbols are never dead, production code called only from tests is not dead (Go included); production code under `test/` or `src/test/` folders and test-annotated files are left out of the analysis.
- A Java file with a `@Test` method counts as a test file anywhere.
- Limits: TypeScript misses union-typed receivers (`Pool | null`), getters returning a pool, namespace imports of relative modules and numeric constants in templates. Java's tree-sitter tier keeps strings only and evaluates no constants; MyBatis `<script>` and `${}` pass through as written; without a binding, subclass receivers, `super.update(...)` and `batchUpdate` array literals are missed. Go's tree-sitter tier decodes interpreted tag literals with JSON rules and reads exported structs only; build-tagged test files are not loaded, so the full tier gives them no symbols; sqlc-style interfaces, method values and method expressions give no call sites; sqlx `...Context` forms are not listed.
- Corpus: `packages/sql-extract/corpus/<case>.<ts|java|go>.fixture` with `mode` `typescript`, `java` or `go`, run only by the matching plugin.

---

## Domain Knowledge Layer: `@ctxo/domain` (0.14.0, #156 PR 2B)

An opt-in package that lets a team name its bounded contexts and keep markdown cards in step with code. Ctxo supplies structure, linkage, verification and retrieval; it never writes domain text or fetches external documentation. Feature doc: docs/features/domain-knowledge.md ("Named contexts and the domain package", "Ctxo domain conventions v1"). Design record: docs/architecture/ADR/adr-018-domain-knowledge-layer.md.

### Install and loading

- `ctxo install domain` installs `@ctxo/domain` at the CLI's version (globally when the project has no `package.json`; `npm i -g @ctxo/cli @ctxo/domain @ctxo/lang-sql` is the supported path for such repositories). `ctxo init --domain` also sets it up.
- The CLI loads the package from the project's `node_modules`, then from next to itself, through `@ctxo/cli/internal` (types only, plus `createModuleHost`). Only a copy at the same `major.minor` loads; `@ctxo/cli` and `@ctxo/domain` share one version.
- Without the package: no domain commands, fields or hooks. A known domain command name (`verify-domain`, `contexts-touched`, `domain`) prints an install hint and exits 1; `ctxo domain-guard-hook` exits 0 without output; `ctxo --help` ends with one install hint line. With the package and no registry: the commands print a hint and exit 0 and no `context` fields appear.

### Registry and cards

- `docs/domain/contexts.yaml` (`domain.registry`): `version: 1`, `contexts[]` with `id` (kebab-case, permanent), `name`, `card` (optional only at rung fear), `paths` (globs), `rung` (fear, pinned, named, bounded, boring), `rulePrefix`, `contracts` (target context to allowed target files); `unowned.allow`, `glossary` (`docs/domain/glossary.md`), `contextMap` (`docs/domain/context-map.md`, a table with Context and Rung columns that must agree with the registry).
- A file belongs to at most one context. Unowned files warn by default (`domain.coverage.unowned: error` to fail).
- Card: five H2 headings in order (Language; Rules and invariants; Boundary contracts; Decisions; Open questions). Rules are `### <ID> <title>` under Rules and invariants, with optional `Tests:`, `Code:` and `Untested:` lines. A rule needs a test link, a `Tests:` line or an `Untested:` line.
- Rule IDs match `domain.rules.idPattern` (default `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+$`), are permanent and unique across cards, and use the context's `rulePrefix` when it has one. A test links to a rule through `[Trait("Rule", "LEND-03")]` (keys in `domain.tests.ruleTraitKeys`), `Category` / `TestCategory` / `Tag` values, `rule: LEND-03` comments, test titles that start with an ID, or the card's `Tests:` line. Tracker prefixes (`domain.rules.trackerPrefixes`) never link from plain text.

### Commands

- `ctxo contexts-touched [--since <ref>] [--committed | --staged] [--json] [--check]`: contexts whose paths hold a changed non-test file, with status `card-changed`, `acknowledged` (a `Domain-Unchanged` trailer in the range), `unresolved` or `no-card`. `--check` exits 1 on unresolved; 2 on registry problems, a missing base (CI needs `fetch-depth: 0`) or git failure.
- `ctxo verify-domain [--since <ref>] [--boundaries by-rung|report] [--json]`: checks 1 registry and config, 2 cards present, 3 path globs match, 4a single owner, 4b unowned files, 5 card headings, 6 rule IDs and test links, 7 card links and anchors, 8 generated loader rules, 9 context map rungs, 10 boundaries, 11 fold since a ref (with `--since`), 12 shadow-spec resolutions (PR 4). Exit 0 (warnings allowed), 1 errors, 2 missing index, git failure or internal error. `--json` writes `{ registry, checks, summary, exitCode }` to stdout; stdout is empty on exit 2 and with no registry.
- `ctxo domain rules --write | --check`: one pointer file per context with a card: `.claude/rules/ctxo-context-<id>.md` (front matter `paths`) and, when `.cursor/` exists, `.cursor/rules/ctxo-context-<id>.mdc`. Marker `<!-- generated by ctxo domain rules; do not edit -->`. `--check` exits 1 on missing, outdated, stale and blocked files (a hand-written file at a generated path; rename or delete it).
- `ctxo domain discover [--json] [--write]`: run it first when adopting or tuning the domain config. Card rule prefixes, tracker-like keys in commit subjects and branch names (5 or more is proposed as a tracker prefix), external IDs (`ADR`, `BIP`, `CAPEC`, `CVE`, `CWE`, `EIP`, `GHSA`, `IEC`, `ISO`, `JSR`, `KEP`, `OWASP`, `PEP`, `RFC`: "references, not rule IDs; no config needed", counted, never proposed, flagged when equal to a card rule prefix; a plain mention never links as a rule ID since only card IDs link; no longer in `trackerKeys`), GitHub issues (issue references in subjects: `#N` at the start, `(#N)`, or after fixes, closes, refs and similar words, with their share and the squash-suffix count, plus `N-slug` branches; named as the issue tracker when at least 5 and the largest family; evidence only), other identifiers (lowercase `name-NN` branch families in 3 or more branches, runtime names left out, marked as a possible tracker key when their upper case is a known prefix; evidence only), test trait keys, uncovered test folders, and test-kind markers (Trait or Category values that equal or end with the kind as `Trait:<Key>=<Value>` annotations, custom attributes such as `StorageContractFact` as annotation names, test files named `*ContractTests`, `*CharacterizationTests`, `*.contract.test.ts` or `*_contract_test.go` as `paths` globs such as `**/*ContractTests.cs`, since `names` match test case names only; a file named after a non-test class is not proposed); `--write` merges the proposal into `.ctxo/config.yaml`, adding values and removing none (remove a wrong value by hand). `--json` adds `externalIds`, `githubIssues`, `otherIdentifiers`, `testKindMarkers`, `characterizationAnnotations` and `contractAnnotations`.
- `ctxo init --domain [--boundaries <by-rung|report>]` or `--only domain`: config defaults, registry skeleton, discovery with confirmation, loader rules, guard hooks (SessionStart, Stop, TaskCompleted) and the `ctxo-domain-fold` skill (Claude Code and Cursor).

### Fold guard and trailer

- `ctxo domain-guard-hook` judges only the commits of the current session (`startHead..HEAD`, recorded at SessionStart, intersected with the branch range from `domain.guard.base`, `origin/HEAD`, `main` or `master`; unpushed commits on the default branch). It blocks once per fingerprint (HEAD plus unresolved IDs): `Stop` prints `{"decision":"block","reason":...}` and exits 0, `TaskCompleted` prints to stderr and exits 2. `stop_hook_active` and every internal error allow.
- Trailer: `Domain-Unchanged: <id>[, <id>...] [(reason)]`, read with `git log --format=%(trailers:key=Domain-Unchanged,valueonly)` over the evaluated range only. A card change in the range also resolves a context. An empty commit with the trailer is fine.

### Boundaries, drift and fields

- `ctxo index` writes `.ctxo/index/domain/contexts.json`, `boundaries.json` and `history/` (10 per-commit entries), each with a `ctxoArtifact` marker that the index reader skips.
- Edges between contexts are allowed when the target file matches the source context's `contracts.<target>`; otherwise a violation: an error for `blockingRungs` (default bounded, boring) in `by-rung` mode, else a warning (`report` mode: always a warning). Edges from test files and to unowned files are skipped.
- Additive fields: `context` (set when exactly one context owns the file) on search_symbols results, get_blast_radius impacted symbols, find_importers importers, get_logic_slice roots and get_pr_impact changed symbols; `contextBoundaryViolations` (capped at 50, with `contextBoundaryViolationsTotal`) on get_pr_impact; `contextDrift` (`crossShare`, `trend`, `movedFiles`, `distinctCommits`, `confidence`) on get_why_context.

### Doctor and global installs

- `domain_registry`, `domain_agent_setup` and `domain_conventions` (all pass or warn; a repo with neither `.claude/` nor `.cursor/` is checked as Claude Code and carries a standing agent-setup warning until `ctxo init --only domain`).
- `install_copies` (every project): warns, never fails, when hooks call `ctxo` and none is on PATH, or an npx-pinned MCP entry differs from the global CLI the hooks run. `ctxo init` from a global install writes MCP entries that call the global `ctxo`.

### Config

`domain:` keys and defaults: `registry: docs/domain/contexts.yaml`, `coverage.unowned: warn`, `boundaries.enforce: by-rung`, `boundaries.blockingRungs: [bounded, boring]`, `rules.idPattern: ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+$`, `rules.trackerPrefixes: []`, `tests.ruleTraitKeys: [Rule]`, `guard.enabled: true`, `guard.base` (unset), `guard.subagents: false`. An invalid key falls back to its default and verify-domain check 1 reports it.

### Adoption ladder

level 0: install and index; 1: registry with paths; 2: cards; 3: rule IDs and test links, through card `Tests:` lines, test names or framework tags; 4: contracts and shadow-spec resolutions. No level requires code changes.

---

## Domain Graph (0.15.0, #156 PR 3)

With `@ctxo/domain` and a registry, `ctxo index` (and the post-commit hook, also for a card-only commit) writes `.ctxo/index/domain/graph.json` (`ctxoArtifact: "domain-graph"`, byte-identical for the same input). `ctxo watch` does not rebuild it. Code metrics never read it.

### Nodes and links
- Nodes: `context:<id>`, `rule:<ID>`, `term:<context>/<term-key>` (repo-wide glossary terms use `*`), `decision:<context>/<date>-<n>`; search-only `section:<card>:<line>`.
- Links, each with `source` and the evidence location `at` (1-based): rule-test (`annotation`: xUnit Trait with a `domain.tests.ruleTraitKeys` key; `category`: NUnit Category, MSTest TestCategory, JUnit Tag; `test-title`; `rule-comment`; `mention`; `card-tests`), rule-symbol (`card-code`; `rule-comment` in indexed non-test files up to 1 MiB, linked to the symbol starting within three lines below when it sits inside the symbol containing the comment, else the innermost one), decision-provenance (`card-link`, `card-text`), decision-rule, term-identifier (`symbol-name`, `table-name`; contiguous token run with plural folding, own context only, at most 50 per term).
- Card values that resolve to nothing are kept in `unresolved` (`missing-file`, `not-a-symbol`).

### Card format additions (Ctxo domain conventions v1)
- `Tests:` and `Code:` values: repo-relative paths or symbol IDs (anything with `::`); `file#Name` names a plain test. A symbol ID the index does not hold links to its file. C# symbol IDs differ between the Roslyn and tree-sitter tiers, so prefer file paths in C# `Code:` lines.
- `**Term**` items in Language; glossary items anywhere in glossary.md, `(context: <id>)` ties one to a context.
- Decision lines `- YYYY-MM-DD: text`; rule IDs written in them link the decision; relative links are provenance files, `#123`, URLs and tracker keys external strings (never fetched).
- An H1 ends the Rules and invariants section. Shared cards: rules belong to the first context by id (warned once).

### Staleness
- Registry changed since the graph: no domain fields, tools answer the "run ctxo index" hint.
- Cards or glossary changed: answers from the graph with `stale: true` and a hint.

### verify-domain check 6
- `<ID>: Code file "<file>" does not exist` (error, also for directories, like Tests).
- `<ID>: <field>: "<value>" is not an indexed symbol; it links to its file` (warning).
- `rule: comment names unknown rule <ID>` (warning, production code, only for a rule prefix).

### Internal API (ADR-018 addendum)
- Async enrichers (awaited by get_blast_radius, get_pr_impact, get_why_context; dropped with a warning by synchronous tools), get_context_for_task as the seventh enrich-seam tool, `reserveTaskContextTokens` (summed, capped at a quarter of tokenBudget), `rankedContextScopes`, host services `createDocumentSearch`, `splitIdentifier`, `dataResourceKinds`.
- The ctxo-domain-fold skill marker was v0.15 in 0.15.0 (v0.16 since PR 4); `ctxo doctor` reports older copies as outdated until `ctxo init --only domain`.

---

## Fact Detectors, the Deletion Test Loop and the Context Map (unreleased, #156 PR 4)

New in the next release. Feature doc: docs/features/domain-knowledge.md (Facts, The Deletion Test loop, The context map and rungs).

### Fact kinds
- `literal-comparison`: a comparison in a condition (if, while, do-while, for, ternary, switch case, when guards, Go tagless switch) with exactly one literal operand that is not trivial (`domain.facts.trivialLiterals`, default `[0, 1, -1, null, true, false, ""]`, typed: `"0"` is not `0`); detail `operator` (`case` for case labels), `literal`.
- `normalization`: a call matching `domain.facts.normalizationMethods` (`Name`, `Name*` prefix, `q.Name` only when written `q.Name(...)`); detail `method`.
- `retry-timeout`: a numeric constant (number literals and `+ - * /`) bound to a name whose ASCII tokens start with retry, retries, attempt, timeout, delay, backoff, ttl or expir (token boundaries: `settlementDays` does not match, a deliberate narrowing of the spec's substring wording), or a duration constructor (`TimeSpan.From*`, `Duration.of*`, `n * time.Second`, `setTimeout(fn, n)`) with units ns, us, ms, s, min, h, d; detail `name`, `value`; text `<name> = <value>`. Not produced in test files.
- `endpoint`: C# `Http*` attributes with the class `[Route]` (`[controller]`, `[action]`, `/` and `~/` templates) and `MapGet`/`MapPost`/`MapPut`/`MapDelete`/`MapPatch`; Nest decorators in exported controllers, Express and Fastify calls on receivers traced to the module; Spring mappings and JAX-RS; `net/http` `HandleFunc`/`Handle` (`"GET /x"` patterns) and gin; detail `verb` (upper case, `ANY` when none), `route`.
- A TypeScript `typeof` guard (`typeof x === 'string'`, `switch (typeof x)`) gives no fact. A fact extraction failure in an official plugin warns on stderr and gives `facts: []`; the detector lists reach plugins as one deep-frozen object (`config.facts`, never mutate it).
- Text single-line, at most 200 code points; at most 500 facts per file; attribution to the innermost declaration or the module symbol `<file>::<basename>::variable`. Rules shared byte for byte by the four plugins (the `@ctxo/domain` copy differs only in its header and imports); `packages/plugin-api/conformance/fact-vectors.json` defines them.

### Tiers
- C#: Roslyn IOperation (`--facts=`) and tree-sitter; TypeScript: ts-morph; Java: JDT (`--facts=`; an older JAR prints `analyzer too old for facts`) and tree-sitter; Go: ctxo-go-analyzer (`--facts=`) and tree-sitter. Tiers agree; C#'s syntax-tier `(n)` suffix is ignored by fingerprints.
- Text fallback (`@ctxo/domain`): indexed files with no `facts` key and tracked files with an extension in `domain.facts.textScanExtensions` (.dart, .ex, .exs, .groovy, .kt, .kts, .php, .py, .rb, .rs, .scala, .swift); single-line heuristics, `source: "text"`; lines over 20,000 UTF-16 code units skipped.
- Upgrade: with `@ctxo/domain` and its registry file, or `index.facts: true`, C#, TypeScript, Java and Go files get `facts` (possibly empty) on the next re-index; without a registry `@ctxo/domain` requests no facts. Run a full `ctxo index` once, and again after adding the registry (old entries without the key get text candidates). The text scan follows a tracked symlink or junction only when its target stays inside the repository.

### Candidates and resolutions
- Candidates: facts of non-test files with one owner (`native` or `text`), owned tables, views and procedures (`index`), rules without tests (`card`). Several may share a fingerprint; counts are per candidate.
- Fingerprint: `kind | symbol | normalized text`; symbol part = last two `.` segments of `<file basename without its last extension>.<symbol name>` without a `(...)` suffix, the file part one segment (`loan.service.ts::withRetry` gives `loan.service.withRetry`, `x.d.ts::x` gives `x.d.x`; the module symbol `<file>::<basename>::variable` gives the basename alone: `app.ts` gives `app`, `api.loan.service.ts` gives `api.loan.service`); a member whose name holds a dot keeps its containing type (`Loan.IComparable<Lending.Loan>.CompareTo`); `%` and `|` in kind and symbol parts are `%25` and `%7C`.
- Resolution order: a rule link (card `Code:` lines, `rule:` comments), an `Untested:` line, then `<registry folder>/<context>/shadow-specs.yaml`: `- fingerprint: '...'` (single-quoted, a `'` written `''`) with `resolution: { rule: LEND-03 }` or `{ notARule: "reason" }`. Schema `packages/domain/schema/shadow-specs.schema.json`. Read on every call. A broken item is skipped (error), a repeated fingerprint warns.

### Rungs and the context map
- pinned: at least `domain.rungs.pinnedCoverage` (0.8) of the main paths (endpoint fact symbols plus contract symbols) reached from characterization tests over calls, uses, imports, extends, implements (no data edges, no HTTP-level reach); without main paths, one characterization test. named: a card whose Language terms (at least one) are all in the glossary. bounded: every contract symbol reached from a contract test and no violations (vacuous with no contract symbols; not met without boundaries.json). boring: every rule tested and no open candidate. Cumulative ladder; every criterion reported.
- K13a conventions: `domain.tests.characterization` and `domain.tests.contract` with `annotations` (`Name`, `Name:value`, `Name:key=value`; defaults `Trait:Kind=Characterization`, `Tag:characterization`, `Trait:Kind=Contract`, `Tag:contract`), `paths` (`**/Characterization/**`; `**/Contract/**`, `**/Contracts.Tests/**`), `names` (`[characterization]`, `[contract]`). `ctxo domain discover` proposes uncovered Characterization and Contract folders; its printed config quotes every list value, so it is valid YAML.

### Commands and artifacts
- `ctxo domain map [--json]`, `ctxo domain shadow-specs <context> [--kinds <k,...>] [--all] [--json]`: the tool bodies without `_meta`; the human output prints each fingerprint single-quoted, ready to paste; exit 0 done (stale data prints a hint and still exits 0) or no registry, 1 bad arguments or unknown context, 2 registry problems, no index data, index data from another registry (`[ctxo] The domain registry changed since the last "ctxo index"; run it to rebuild the domain graph.`) or an internal error (`[ctxo] domain <name> failed: <message>`). Repeated `--kinds` options add up.
- `ctxo verify-domain` check 12: unparsable shadow-specs.yaml error; stale entries, unknown rules, orphan files warn; computed from current inputs. When the candidates cannot be built and some file has entries: one warning `stale resolutions were not checked: <reason>` (exit stays 0).
- `.ctxo/index/domain/shadow-candidates.json` and `maturity.json` (markers `domain-shadow-candidates`, `domain-maturity`), written by `ctxo index`, not by `ctxo watch`. Both written or both removed: when the graph builds but the candidates or maturity facts fail, both marked files are removed (with a warning) and the tools answer "run ctxo index"; when the graph build fails, graph.json and both files stay as they were.
- Known limits (full list in the feature doc): evidence cap of 2,000 per file in every tier but TypeScript, counting trivial comparisons, in walk order (tiers can differ above it); Roslyn facts in a second field declarator have no symbol; TypeScript constructor parameter defaults give no fact; an old Java analyzer JAR gives only annotation endpoints; Go watch takes a saved file's facts from tree-sitter, a file created during watch gets `facts: []` until the next ctxo index; whitespace inside string literals is collapsed in fingerprints; incremental runs after installing @ctxo/domain, adding the registry or changing the fact lists mix native and text facts until a full ctxo index; a ctxo watch started before the registry existed keeps facts off until restarted; test-case classification is quadratic per test file; a domain graph build failure makes verify-domain exit 2 before checks 1 to 11.
- Internal API: `indexCapabilities.factOptions` (handed to plugins as `PluginContext.config.facts`), host service `readCoChangeEntries(ctxoRoot)`; truncatable `shadowSpecs`, `contextMap`. Skill marker v0.16.

---

## Safe-Edit Guard (v0.8+)

The safe-edit guard closes the loop between MCP tool availability and agent compliance. An agent with access to get_blast_radius can still skip it. The guard makes skipping impossible for high-impact symbols on Claude Code.

### How it works

`ctxo init` registers a PreToolUse hook in `.claude/settings.json`:
```json
{ "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [{ "matcher": "Edit", "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "ctxo gate-hook" }] }] } }
```

On every Edit call, `ctxo gate-hook` checks whether get_blast_radius has been called for that symbol in the current session. If not, the hook blocks the edit and returns a message: "High-impact symbol - run get_blast_radius first." Once the agent calls the tool, the edit goes through. Fires once per symbol per session. Fail-open on any error.

- Matcher `Edit` only: `ctxo gate-hook` ignores every other tool, so `Write` (new files, whole-file rewrites) and `NotebookEdit` are not gated.
- Session state is a file store: the hook runs as a new process per Edit call, records the symbols it already warned about in `.ctxo/.cache/gate/<session_id>.json`, and also accepts a get_blast_radius call found in the session transcript. It survives MCP server restarts.
- A `.claude/settings.json` that is not valid JSON (JSONC comments included) or not a settings object is never overwritten; `ctxo init` warns and leaves it. The guard is also detected in `.claude/settings.local.json` (read only).

### Gate decision

A symbol is flagged if it exceeds both thresholds:
- Blast radius: confirmed + likely dependents >= minDependents floor
- PageRank percentile: symbol falls in top N% of the codebase by centrality

Sensitivity levels (configured in `.ctxo/config.yaml`):
- `strict`: top 30%, floor 2
- `balanced` (default): top 15%, floor 3
- `lenient`: top 5%, floor 5

### New CLI commands

- `ctxo blast-radius <symbolId> --json` - compute blast radius for one symbol, JSON to stdout
- `ctxo gate --preview [--json]` - show which symbols would be flagged at current sensitivity

### Skills

Three model-invoked skill files installed to `.claude/skills/` (Claude Code) and `.cursor/rules/` (Cursor):
- `ctxo-understand`: run get_context_for_task at the start of a task, and pick the right tool for a structural question from a question-to-tool table that covers all 14 tools (reading a file to see its contents needs no index call)
- `ctxo-safe-edit`: run get_blast_radius and get_why_context before any edit
- `ctxo-review-pr`: run get_pr_impact before reviewing a diff

### Platform support

| Platform | Hook enforcement | Skills | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Yes (PreToolUse) | Yes | Yes |
| Cursor | No (no blocking pre-edit hook in v3.6) | Yes | Yes |
| Other platforms | No | Where supported | Yes |

### Tiered rules (v0.13, #159)

`ctxo init` writes one ctxo block into each AI tool's rules file, between `<!-- ctxo-rules-start v<version> -->` and `<!-- ctxo-rules-end -->`. The version is the rules template version, the CLI minor in which the rules text last changed.

- Compact tier, Claude Code only (`CLAUDE.md`, 4 lines of text; at most 8 non-blank lines including the markers, 6 today): written when the guard hook is registered (`.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`), all three skills are in `.claude/skills/`, and `gate.enabled` is not false. It says the repo has a ctxo index, to use the ctxo tools for structural questions before grepping, that the guard blocks the first edit to a high-impact symbol until get_blast_radius is called, and names the three skills.
- Full tier: every other client, Claude Code without one of those three, and a rules file several clients share (an `AGENTS.md` or `GEMINI.md` that is a hard link or a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`). First rule: "For structural questions (dependencies, impact, history), use ctxo tools first; reading a file to see its contents needs no index call." Then the tool guide; its modification steps end with "Only then edit the source".
- The tier follows the disk after the skills and guard steps; `--no-guard` and `--skip skills` give the full block unless the guard and skills are already installed (they remove nothing).
- The domain line (#191): when the domain layer is set up (a `domain` key in `.ctxo/config.yaml` or the default registry `docs/domain/contexts.yaml`, both committed; otherwise a loaded `@ctxo/domain`), both tiers add "Adopting or tuning the domain layer? Run `ctxo domain discover` first (`--json` for the evidence, `--write` to merge the proposal)." (the compact block's last line, 7 non-blank lines with the markers; the full block's last bullet under "Orientation in Unfamiliar Areas"). Committed state decides first, so teammates with and without the package render the same block, and a machine where the module fails to load keeps the line. Without domain state and module the block is byte-identical to before and the template version stays 0.13 (a pre-#191 ctxo treats the line as an edit and removes it). `ctxo init --domain` renders the rules again when the domain step set the layer up; `ai_rules` warns on a block that lacks the line while the layer is set up, or has it while it is not, and `doctor --fix` re-renders it.
- Re-runs replace the first ctxo block in place (versioned, unversioned `<!-- ctxo-rules-start -->`, or the old unmarked body), collapse later blocks into it, and keep every byte outside the blocks, including a UTF-8 BOM and CRLF line endings. Create-mode files (`.cursor/rules/ctxo.mdc`, `AGENTS.md` and the rest) keep user content. A block from a newer ctxo, a start marker without an end marker, or an end marker without a start marker leaves the file unchanged with a warning.
- Formatter stable: blocks and skills are written in the layout Prettier prints, and blocks, the old unmarked body and skills are compared with formatting ignored (line endings, BOM, trailing whitespace, blank lines, table padding; blocks and skills also ignore line wrapping, so `proseWrap: always` or `never` is no edit). A block a formatter reshaped is current and `unchanged`, and the tier is read from the first non-blank line. The compact tier counts a skill only when it is readable and current. A rules file ctxo cannot read is left unchanged with one warning, and init goes on.
- Held blocks: init (real run, dry run, `--only rules`, `--rules`) and `ctxo doctor --fix` leave `CLAUDE.md` or `.cursor/rules/ctxo.mdc` unchanged when its block is pre-tier or compact, the user has not declined the guard or skills (`--no-guard`, the guard question answered no, `gate.enabled: false`, `--skip skills`), and after the skills and guard steps they are still not on disk (an unreadable `.claude/settings.json` counts as no guard). Init warns `<file>: left unchanged until the guard and skills are installed; run "ctxo init --only rules,skills,guard" or "ctxo doctor --fix"`; the dry run prints `unchanged (held)`. A file linked to a held one is held too. A file without a ctxo block is never held.
- Skills carry a version marker, `<!-- ctxo-skill v<version> -->` (SKILLS_TEMPLATE_VERSION). An installed skill with a newer marker is left alone with a warning and is not outdated; no marker or an older one is outdated and replaced.

### Granular init (v0.13, #159)

- Parts, run in this order: `config` (`.ctxo/config.yaml`, `.gitignore` entry, `.ctxo/index/`), `skills`, `guard`, `rules`, `mcp`, `git-hooks`.
- `ctxo init --only <parts>` installs exactly those parts (and skips the plugin step); `ctxo init --skip <parts>` installs the rest (the plugin step still runs); `ctxo init --no-guard` does not install the guard and never asks. `-y` without `--tools` sets up all nine tools, the same set the dry run previews. `--only` cannot be combined with `--skip` or `--rules`; an unknown part exits 1.
- `ctxo init --rules` is deprecated: the same as `--skip git-hooks,guard`, prints a notice, and still skips the plugin step.
- The interactive guard question appears only when Claude Code is selected. Cursor gets the skills and the full block, but no guard question and no hook.
- `ctxo init --dry-run` lists every file init would create or change (`would create`, `would update`, `unchanged`) and writes nothing.
- Init output: `[ctxo] ✓ <file> (<created|updated|unchanged>)`, warnings as `[ctxo] ⚠ <text>`.

### Agent-setup doctor checks (v0.13, #159)

- `ai_rules`: an outdated block (unversioned, older template, or edited), a `CLAUDE.md` block that expects the guard while it is missing, a current block in the wrong tier, several blocks in one file, a start marker without an end marker, an end marker without a start marker. A block from a newer ctxo passes, and so does a file with no ctxo block. Linked files are reported once.
- `skills`: missing or outdated ctxo skills for Claude Code and Cursor, where expected (one ctxo skill installed, or the rules block is pre-tier or compact). Formatting is ignored, and a skill from a newer ctxo is not reported.
- `claude_guard_hook`: an unreadable `.claude/settings.json`, or a missing guard while the `CLAUDE.md` block expects it and the gate is enabled.
- All three warn, never fail. A versioned full block and `gate.enabled: false` are opt-outs and pass.
- `ctxo doctor --fix` order: Config, Git hooks, Skills, Claude guard hook, AI rules, then plugins, index and cache. AI rules re-render whenever any of the three checks warned, so the tier follows the fixes. A block is held unchanged by the same rule as init while the guard or the skills it expects are not in place (unreadable settings, failed install); doctor keeps reporting them until fixed. The Skills step reports a skill from a newer ctxo as a warning line and fails on a skill path it cannot write. `--fix` never installs what the user declined, never writes an unreadable `.claude/settings.json`, and replaces edited ctxo skills with the bundled copy (copy a customised skill under another name).

Design record: docs/architecture/ADR/adr-015-safe-edit-guard.md (amendment: tiered rules)
